 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar, S/o B.G.Thambrahall, in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 27.12.2023 at about 07.10 p.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-35-EB-8689 from Kondanayanakahalli to Hosapete and when he reached in front of Shrikari College Cross Road,
Hosapete, Vijanagara, Karnataka, a rider of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH-45-AK-2474, drove the vehicle at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased.
Due to the accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Hosapete and then to Vims Hospital, Bellary and he succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.

Later, the body was taken to Vijanagar Institute of Medical Science, Bellary, wherein postmortem was conducted and petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.4,50,000/- towards the funeral, obsequies and transportation of dead body.

sentences.text:
Prior to the accident,
the deceased was hale and healthy and was an employee and doing business and earning a sum of .50,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the rider of Unicorn motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

Further respondent No.2 denied the aspect of issue of policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in respect of motor cycle and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that as on the date of accident the petitioner sustained injuries due to hit and run by an unknown vehicle which is very much evident from the complaint lodged at very belated stage before the police.
Further contended that as on the date of accident the motor cycle was being ridden by its rider in a Rathna T vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025

Further the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-35-EB-8689 did not possess the DL and the owner of vehicle handed over the vehicle to the person who did not possess valid DL at the time of accident.

Further the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner himself who was fallen from the motor cycle while proceeding near Hospet Vijayanagara road on the middle of the busy road without having proper look out for vehicular movements on the road and without noticing the oncoming vehicles, suddenly tried crossing the road without observation and due to this the deceased fell on his own and not due to any negligence on the part of motor cycle.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:

ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 27.12.2023 at about 07.10 p.m.,
infront of Shrikari College Cross Road, Hosapete, Vijayanagara, Karnataka, when deceased was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-35- EB-8689 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH-45-AK-2474 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner/son of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and one eye witness by name Sri.J.S.Channaveerappa got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his side of evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Deputy Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed his side of evidence.

7. Heard arguments of both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 : As per final order, for  the following:

sentences.text: 10. The Petitioner/son of deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar examined as PW.1.
In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that his father was proceeding as a pillion rider and due to the rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider, the accident occurred.
In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of container motorcycle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2
First Information lodged by one Sri.J.S.Chennaverappa S/o Sri.J.C.Sharana Basappa with police on 28.12.2023 with respect to the accident occurred on 27.12.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and U/s.183 of M.V.Act.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar & sketch which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
Ex.P5 - IMV Report, wherein damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages caused to offending vehicle.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages were caused to the vehicle.
The respondents disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
But, the IMV report discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut the said document or substantiate that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is the Inquest Report.
Ex.P8 is the PM report, wherein it is mentioned that the deceased Sri.Ashwin Kumar died due to "Intra Cranial Hemorrhage" as a result of head injury sustained.

The I.O., after detailed investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337, 338 & 304(A) and U/s.183 of of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
In the final report, there is no mention about negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle in which the deceased was traveling.
The documents furnished by petitioner disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle by its rider in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioner related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or rider of the offending motor cycle does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the rider of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
The petitioner got examined eye witness to the accident as PW.2.
PW.2 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.1 and in the cross examination of PW.2 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioner could be elicited from the witness.
The documents furnished by petitioner is corroborated and substantiated by evidence of PW.2.
PW.2 stated the aspect of occurrence of accident and negligence of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
PW.2 not stated the aspect of negligence of rider of motorcycle in which the deceased was going, in the cause of accident.

Nothing to substantiate the contention of respondents could be Rathna T vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47693188/
4 elicited from the witness during cross examination.

sentences.text: The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.

Though the respondent No.1 contended about negligence on the part of rider of vehicle bearing registration number KA-35-EB-8689, no cogent and substantive materials are placed before the Tribunal in that regard.
The contention regarding negligence of rider of motorcycle bearing registration number KA- 35-EB-8689, is not substantiated by any satisfactory materials.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of rider of offending motor cycle in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioner coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH- 45-AK-2474 by its rider and deceased succumbed to injuries.

Accordingly,
Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.
(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings: (i) In the petition, the age of the deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar is shown as 43 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioner has produced Notarized copy of DL and Aadhaar Card, wherein date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 02.06.1981.
The accident occurred on 27.12.2023.
As per the documents furnished by petitioner, the age of the deceased appears to be 43 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 43 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case '14' multiplier is applicable in the present case.
(ii) The petitioner contended that deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar was working as an employee and was doing business and earning a sum of .50,000/- per month.

In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - IT Returns for the assessment year 2014-15 and 2015-16 and also produced authorization letter issued by D.Rajashekhar, Class 1 Contractor, which is marked at Ex.P.10.
In order to prove the said contention, the petitioner has not examined the author of the said document.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income of deceased.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.

sentences.text: Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioner is entitled for future prospects.

In National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 25% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was aged between 40 to 50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 43 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 25% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased is .16,000/- and 25% of .16,000/-
is .4,000/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .16,000/- + .4,000/- = .20,000/- per month.
As per the materials on record, the deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar is married, having son.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has produced notarized copy of Aadhaar card, which is marked as Ex.P11.
On perusal of the same it reveals that petitioner is the son of deceased.
The said document discloses the aspect of relationship of deceased with that of the petitioner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to disprove or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to his relationship with that of the deceased.
As per the materials on record, the petitioner is the son of deceased and he is considered to be the dependent of deceased.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the petitioner was not dependent on the income of deceased.
Hence, the petitioner is the only dependent of deceased.
In MFA No.20759/2012 in case of Smt.Geeta V/s Smt.Sundarawwa and others, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held in its judgment at para N.8 as follows:

The arguments as regard the deduction towards personal expenses in the case of sole dependent is based on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the deduction towards personal expenses should be 1/3rd when the dependents of the deceased are either two or three, 1/4th if the dependents are between 4 and 6 and 1/5th if the dependents are more than 6.

A coordinate bench of this Court has considered this question of deduction towards personal expenses if the deceased is survive by a sole dependent in the light of the decision in Sarla Verma's case referred supra and deducted 50%
towards personal expenses.

This court can only agree with the submissions by the learned counsel for the Insurer that the deduction towards personal expenses in the case of a sole dependent should be 50% (or 1/2) of the Income as it stands to reason that if the permissible deduction in the case the number of dependents is either 2 or 3 should be 1/3rd, the deduction cannot be the same if the deceased is survived by a sole dependent.
Of the two claimants, the claimant is the wife and the other claimant is a major son.
Therefore, only the wife would qualify as the dependent.
As such the deduction towards personal expenses should be 50% ( or 1/2) of the income.

As such, the argument by the learned counsel for Rathna T vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47693188/
6 the Insurer in this regard is accepted."

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs of the said judgment reads as under:
"30.

Though in some cases the deduction to be made towards personal and living expenses is calculated on the basis of units indicated in Trilok Chandra, the general practice is to apply standardized deductions.

Having considered several subsequent decisions of this court, we are of the view that where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, should be one-third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members 2 to 3, one- fourth(1/4th)
where the number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, and one-fifty (1/5th) where the number of dependent family members exceeds six.
This implies that when there is only one dependent of the deceased, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be taken as 1/2."
This Tribunal has carefully perused the above judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The ratio and dictums laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka is aptly applicable to the case on hand since there is only one dependent of deceased in the present case.

So, in view of the above reported judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of deceased should be taken as 1/2.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH-45-AK- 2474.
The materials on record disclose that respondent No.2 is the owner of offending vehicle.
Respondent No.1 denied the aspect of issue of policy of insurance pertaining to the vehicle.
Though respondent No.1 denied the issue of policy, they have furnished the policy of insurance which is marked as Ex.R.2.

Ex.R.2 discloses the aspect of issue of policy by respondent No.1 in favour of respondent No.2 pertaining to offending vehicle and also discloses that the policy was valid and effective at the time of accident.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of existence of valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.

opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.T.Ashwin Kumar succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 27.12.2023 at about 07.10 p.m.,
infront of Shrikari College Cross Road, Hosapete, Vijayanagara, Karnataka, when deceased was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-35- EB-8689 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH-45-AK-2474 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The documents furnished by petitioner disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle by its rider in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioner related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or rider of the offending motor cycle does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the rider of offending vehicle.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
Though the respondent No.1 contended about negligence on the part of rider of vehicle bearing registration number KA-35-EB-8689, no cogent and substantive materials are placed before the Tribunal in that regard.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioner coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.MH- 45-AK-2474 by its rider and deceased succumbed to injuries.
The accident occurred on 27.12.2023.
As per the documents furnished by petitioner, the age of the deceased appears to be 43 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 43 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income of deceased.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.
